runs.narrative: I am a young man named Alex. I recently moved into this nursery. The nursery has a collection of trays filled with dry compost that were previously stored in crates. There is also a wooden door leading to the furnace, which emits a warm glow as it warms up during winter. The colonnade around the house stretches eastward, connecting me to other parts of the world. Despite my lack of possessions, I have taken a small step back from the bustling activities of modern life by spending time in this peaceful corner of the earth.

I am a young woman named Emily, exploring an old wooden nursery. The room contains only a trowel, twine, and the remains of a broken window, which has given me clues about the past. The nursery is located near the furnace, where the children would gather for playtime before the day begins. As I walk through the treacherous path between windows, my eyes catch sight of a faint pattern left by the previous owner's mark. This memory serves as both a source of comfort and a reminder of the time spent here with my family.

runs.narrative: I am an elderly man with experience in gardening. In the nursery, I find my tools at ease when working with compost. The ground is cracked, so I use my trowel to loosen it for easy access to the compost. The passage of time has left me somewhat rusty from lack of exercise but also more seasoned by years of experience. My hands feel smooth as they work on the twine that holds the trays together. It's interesting how nature shapes these simple tools into something so useful.
